sections.heading: Driveway & Laneway Base Prep for Farm, Rural & Large-Lot Properties
sections.body: Bellhouse Excavating prepares farm laneways, rural driveways, and large-lot access roads across Brantford and Brant County. We shape the grade, remove unsuitable material, place granular base, and compact the surface so the finished area has better drainage and durability. This page is for farm access roads, rural property driveways, and large-lot grading — not short urban residential driveways.

sections.heading: When This Prep Work Is Worth Bringing Bellhouse In
sections.subheading: Best fit for surfaces that need more than a quick top-up and actually require grade correction, stable base, and proper compaction before the next layer goes down.

cards.title: Driveway rebuilds with soft spots or drainage issues
cards.body: A practical fit when an existing driveway is holding water, rutting, or breaking down because the grade and base underneath were never corrected properly.
cards.outcome: Addresses the underlying grade and base problem instead of just dressing up the surface for a short-term fix.

cards.title: Widening jobs and fresh granular base installs
cards.body: Useful when the work includes cutting back edges, importing stone, placing base in lifts, and tying new prep into an existing driveway or lane cleanly.
cards.outcome: Leaves a more uniform driving surface that is ready for gravel use or handoff to your surface contractor without patchwork transitions.

cards.title: Small parking areas and contractor-ready prep
cards.body: A strong fit for parking lots, yard entrances, and other traffic areas that need usable slopes, compacted base, and a clear handoff to your chosen surface contractor.
cards.outcome: Creates a surface that is easier for the next crew to pave, top, or finish without regrading on arrival.

sections.heading: Best Fit & Not the Best Fit
sections.subheading: Bellhouse driveway and lot prep works best on rural properties, farm laneways, and large lots where there is room for equipment and trucks to work safely.

items.title: Best fit: Farm laneways and rural driveways
items.body: Long laneways, farm access roads, and rural property driveways where the grade, base, and drainage all need proper attention before gravel or surface material goes down.

items.title: Best fit: Large-lot parking areas and yard entrances
items.body: Commercial yard entrances, farm parking areas, and large-lot turnarounds that need grading, compacted base, and a clean handoff to the surface contractor.

items.title: Not the best fit: Short urban residential driveways
items.body: Bellhouse is set up for rural laneways, farm driveways, and large-lot access roads. Short suburban or city driveways with limited space for trucks and equipment are better suited to a smaller-scale contractor.

items.title: Not the best fit: Surface paving or asphalt work
items.body: Bellhouse prepares the base, grade, and compaction. The finished surface — asphalt, concrete, or interlocking — is handled by your chosen surface contractor.

factors.title: Existing grade and soft spots
factors.body: Driveways that are holding water, rutting, or sitting on weak subgrade take more material removal and base work to correct properly.

factors.title: Granular base required
factors.body: The type and depth of imported granular material is a major cost driver. A-gravel, B-gravel, and compacted base all affect material and truck costs.

factors.title: Area size and length
factors.body: Longer laneways, wider parking areas, and larger footprints require more material, machine time, and compaction passes.

factors.title: Drainage and ditching
factors.body: Jobs that need slope correction, edge ditching, or drainage swales add to the scope beyond standard base prep.

factors.title: Site access and obstacles
factors.body: Overhead lines, tight approaches, steep slopes, and the need to work around existing structures all affect how the prep work can be done.

sections.body: Bellhouse focuses on the base, grade, drainage, and compaction before the finished surface goes down. That is what keeps a driveway or parking area from becoming soft, rutted, or uneven soon after the work is done.

sections.heading: What Proper Base Prep Helps Prevent
sections.subheading: Most driveway and parking lot failures start with poor drainage, weak base, or rushed compaction.

items.problem: Soft spots and rutting can return quickly if unsuitable material is left under the surface.
items.solution: Bellhouse removes weak areas where needed and builds the base in a more controlled way.

items.problem: Flat or poorly shaped surfaces can hold water and break down the finished driveway.
items.solution: Grades are shaped with water movement in mind before gravel or the finished surface layer goes down.

items.problem: Loose base material can settle, shift, and leave the next crew correcting avoidable problems.
items.solution: Granular material is placed and compacted so the surface is ready for use or handoff.

items.question: What base material do you recommend?
items.answer: Granular A is common for many rural and farm driveway and surface-prep projects, while Granular B may be used for deeper fills or heavier traffic areas. The right material depends on depth, drainage, use, and site conditions.

items.question: Do you do the gravel base preparation before paving?
items.answer: Yes — we prepare and grade the base layer. The surface paving is handled by your paving contractor. Bellhouse focuses on the excavation, grading, and granular base so the site is ready for whoever is finishing the surface.

items.question: Can you fix driveway drainage issues?
items.answer: Yes. Slope correction, ditching, base repair, and edge shaping can all be part of driveway or parking area prep when drainage is contributing to soft spots or washouts.

items.question: Can you supply the gravel too?
items.answer: Yes. Bellhouse can coordinate aggregate delivery with the grading and base-prep work so material, trucking, and machine time are aligned.
